mainTopic: More תנאים who hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם (a person can transfer something not yet in existence or not yet his): רבי, from the פסוק about a runaway slave, and רבי מאיר, from a ברייתא about conditional קידושין.
overview: The גמרא continues its list of תנאים who hold that a person can transfer something not yet in the world. It counts רבי, who reads the פסוק about a runaway slave as a case where the buyer freed the slave before buying him. It also counts רבי מאיר, who holds that a woman betrothed 'after' a block is removed, such as a conversion or a husband's death, is betrothed. רבי יהודה הנשיא is not added separately, because he is the same person as 'רבי'. רבי עקיבא is not added either, because his vow case is about her hands, which already exist. Next comes a new משנה about betrothal on condition that the man speaks for the woman to the authorities or works for her. ריש לקיש says a separate פרוטה must also be given. Two ברייתות seem to refute him, but he answers that they follow a different view about when a worker's pay becomes owed. רבא adds that the משנה's words 'על מנת' forced his reading. A third משנה deals with betrothal on condition that the man's father agrees, and the גמרא begins asking what that condition means. Its answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי explains the verse about not returning a slave
steps.stepSummary: רבי says the פסוק 'Do not hand over a slave to his master' is about someone who bought a slave in order to free him.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the verse 'You shall not hand over a slave to his master,' רבי says: the verse is talking about someone who buys a slave in order to free him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי as another תנא who holds that a person can transfer something not yet his. He reads the פסוק as being about a slave whose new owner had already freed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי reads 'his master' as a buyer who has no real right to keep the slave, because the slave is already free. That only works if the freeing could take effect before the buyer owned him. That is the idea of אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not hand over (a slave back to his master)
In order to free him
The פסוק is speaking about
Plain 'רבי' with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא

phrases.english: "You shall not hand over a slave to his master"
Rabbi says:
phrases.notes: When the גמרא just says 'רבי' it means רבי יהודה הנשיא. Keep this in mind for the end of the section.

phrases.english: about one who buys a slave in order to free him
the verse is speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: בְּלוֹקֵחַ עֶבֶד עַל מְנָת לְשַׁחְרְרוֹ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from the previous amud of תנאים who hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is about a slave bought in order to be freed, so the buyer may not keep him.

steps.title: What exactly is the case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how such a case actually happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the circumstances?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the exact case behind רבי's reading. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the buyer frees the slave only after buying him, it is simply a normal freeing. The גמרא wants to know what situation makes the buyer 'not allowed' to keep the slave in a way the פסוק needs to say.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What is the exact case?

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the concrete case behind רבי's reading of the פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The concrete scenario of 'buying a slave in order to free him.'

steps.title: Freeing the slave before buying him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says the buyer wrote to the slave: 'When I buy you, you own yourself from now.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: For example, where he wrote to him: 'When I buy you, you are hereby acquired to yourself from now.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives the case. The buyer gave the slave his freedom in writing before he even owned him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At the moment of writing, the buyer did not own the slave, so he was giving away something not yet his. Since רבי says the slave goes free, רבי must hold that a person can transfer something not yet in his hands. This is why רבי belongs on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: When I buy you
Your own self belongs to you (you are free)
From now

steps.whatToRemember: רבי holds אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם: a slave freed by a document written before the purchase goes free.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
For example, where he wrote to him:
"When I buy you,
your own self is hereby acquired to you from now."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: כְּגוֹן דִּכְתַב לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of what the case is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The buyer wrote a document of freedom before buying the slave, meant to take effect once he buys him.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: betrothal that starts after a block is removed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a man betroths a woman 'after' something happens (conversion, freedom, a death, חליצה). The תנא קמא says she is not betrothed; רבי מאיר says she is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר also holds this, as it was taught: One who says to a woman, 'You are betrothed to me after I convert,' 'after you convert,' 'after I am freed,' 'after you are freed,' 'after your husband dies,' 'after your sister dies,' 'after your יבם does חליצה for you,' she is not betrothed. רבי מאיר says: She is betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds רבי מאיר to the list and brings a ברייתא as proof. In every case the man cannot marry her right now, but he betroths her for later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In all these cases the קידושין cannot take effect today, so the man is giving something that is not yet able to happen. The תנא קמא says it does not work. רבי מאיר says it does, which shows he holds אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
Betrothed
That I convert
That I am freed (from slavery)
Your יבם, the brother of your late husband

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying the קידושין work right now. He says they take effect later, once the block (conversion, the husband's death, and so on) is gone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir, as it was taught:
One who says to a woman:
"You are hereby betrothed to me
after I convert," "after you convert,"
"after I am freed," "after you are freed,"
"after your husband dies," "after your sister dies,"
phrases.notes: He is married to her sister, so he cannot marry her while her sister is alive.

phrases.english: "after your yavam does chalitza for you" —
she is not betrothed.
Rabbi Meir says: She is betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new תנא to the list after finishing רבי.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי מאיר says קידושין made to take effect after a future change do work.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says she is not betrothed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן הסנדלר says: She is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with another opinion. רבי יוחנן הסנדלר sides against רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with the first opinion that these future קידושין do not work. This adds weight to the side that says a person cannot give something that is not yet able to take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, a student of רבי עקיבא; 'הסנדלר' means 'the sandal-maker'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says:
She is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר אוֹמֵר: אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further opinion inside the same ברייתא, disagreeing with רבי מאיר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The future קידושין do not take effect.

steps.title: רבי יהודה הנשיא: betrothed, but the חכמים worried about bad feelings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה הנשיא says she is betrothed. The reason the חכמים said 'not betrothed' is to avoid איבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה הנשיא says: She is betrothed. And why did they say 'she is not betrothed'? Because of enmity.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבי יהודה הנשיא's view. He says the קידושין do work, and the ruling against them came from a worry about causing bad feelings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view the קידושין work in principle, so he too holds a person can transfer something not yet possible. The 'not betrothed' ruling is a protective step: promising to marry a woman once her husband or sister dies could stir up hatred between them.

keyTerms.meaning: The editor of the משנה, usually just called 'רבי'
For what reason?
Enmity, bad feelings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: She is betrothed.
And for what reason did they say "she is not betrothed"?
Because of enmity.
phrases.notes: For example, a promise to marry a woman once her husband dies could make bad feelings between her and her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא אוֹמֵר: מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת. וּמָה טַעַם אָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last opinion in the ברייתא, which explains the 'not betrothed' ruling as a protective step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In principle she is betrothed; 'not betrothed' was said only to prevent איבה.

steps.title: Why not also count רבי יהודה הנשיא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה הנשיא is not added to the list, since he also says 'betrothed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us also count רבי יהודה הנשיא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list. רבי יהודה הנשיא also said 'she is betrothed,' so why was he left off?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list named רבי מאיר from this ברייתא, but רבי יהודה הנשיא said the same thing there. It looks like the list is missing a name.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us also count

phrases.english: And let us also count Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the list based on the last opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of תנאים who hold אדם מקנה דבר שלא בא לעולם.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה הנשיא also rules 'betrothed,' so he should be counted as an extra name.

steps.title: רבי and רבי יהודה הנשיא are the same person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'רבי' from the slave פסוק is רבי יהודה הנשיא, so he is already on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי is the same as רבי יהודה הנשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that he was already counted. 'רבי' from step 1 and 'רבי יהודה הנשיא' are one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list is not missing anyone. The ברייתא calls him by his full name, while the slave teaching calls him just 'רבי', but it is the same תנא, already counted once.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as

steps.whatToRemember: The list now includes רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא) and רבי מאיר as holding a person can transfer something not yet in existence. 'רבי' and 'רבי יהודה הנשיא' are one person.

phrases.english: That is Rabbi;
that is Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
phrases.notes: He was already counted back in step 1, from the slave פסוק.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ רַבִּי, הַיְינוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הַנָּשִׂיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by identifying the two names as one person.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identification: two names refer to the same תנא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה הנשיא is a separate name missing from the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is רבי, who was already counted from the slave פסוק.

steps.title: Should רבי עקיבא also be on the list?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests adding רבי עקיבא to the list. In a case of a נדר, he seems to hold that a vow can take effect on work that does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us also count רבי עקיבא. We learned: if a wife says 'What I produce for you is קונם (forbidden to you),' the husband does not need to cancel it. רבי עקיבא says he should cancel it, because maybe she will do more work for him than she owes him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the list of those who say something not yet in the world can be acted on does not also include רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wife already owes her husband her basic work, so a vow cannot forbid that work. רבי עקיבא worries about extra work beyond what she owes, and that extra work does not exist yet. If his concern means the vow can take hold of that future extra work, then he holds like the others on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A word used in vows that makes something forbidden, like a קרבן
To cancel (a vow), which a husband can do for his wife
She will do extra, more than she has to
What he is entitled to

phrases.english: And let us also count Rabbi Akiva,
as it is taught: 'What I produce for you is konam'
he does not need to nullify it.
Rabbi Akiva says: He should nullify it,
since perhaps she will do extra for him
beyond what is due to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 8 placed רבי יהודה הנשיא on the list, the גמרא suggests one more name.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of those who allow acting on something not yet in the world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's worry about future extra work suggests that a vow can take hold of something not yet in existence, so he should be on the list.

steps.title: No, her vow was on her hands, which exist
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע already explained that the woman consecrated her hands, and her hands already exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it already said about this: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said, the case is where she says 'Let my hands be consecrated to their Maker,' and hands exist in the world.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the idea of adding רבי עקיבא, using an explanation that was already given about his case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vow takes hold of her hands themselves, and they already exist, not of future work. So רבי עקיבא's ruling says nothing about something not yet in the world, and he does not belong on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already stated about it?
Let my hands be consecrated to their Maker
They exist in the world

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא is not added to the list, because his case is about hands that already exist.

phrases.english: But wasn't it stated about it,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
It is where she says: 'Let my hands be consecrated to their Maker,'
and hands exist in the world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects adding רבי עקיבא to the list
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion assumed the vow was on future work, but it was actually on her existing hands.

steps.title: משנה: Betrothal on condition he speaks for her or works for her
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה. If a man betroths a woman on condition that he speaks to the authorities for her or works for her as a laborer, she is betrothed if he does it, and not betrothed if he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says to a woman: 'You are betrothed to me on condition that I speak for you to the authorities,' or 'and that I will work for you as a laborer.' If he spoke for her to the authorities and worked for her as a laborer, she is betrothed. If not, she is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It deals with קידושין that depends on a condition about something the man will do for her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קידושין is tied to a condition. Whether she is betrothed depends on whether he actually does the promised service. The משנה does not say what the betrothal item is, and the גמרא will ask about that next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה
On condition that
The government authorities
A hired worker

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who says to a woman:
'You are hereby betrothed to me
on condition that I speak on your behalf to the authorities,'
'and that I will work for you as a laborer,'
if he spoke on her behalf to the authorities
and worked for her as a laborer, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר לָאִשָּׁה הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת לִי עַל מְנָת שֶׁאֲדַבֵּר עָלַיִךְ לַשִּׁלְטוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The previous discussion has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Betrothal on condition of a service takes effect only if the service is done.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: Only if he also gave her a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that the משנה is talking about a case where the man also gave her something worth a פרוטה. The service is only the condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: This is only when he gave her something worth a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. ריש לקיש limits it to a case where a שוה פרוטה was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to ריש לקיש, the speaking or the work does not itself make the קידושין. The פרוטה does that, and the service is only a condition attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: Something worth at least a פרוטה, the smallest amount of money
And this is only when

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Reish Lakish said:
And this is only when he gave her something worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ וְהוּא שֶׁנָּתַן לָהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case of the משנה in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The service is only a condition. The קידושין happens through a separate שוה פרוטה.

steps.title: Can't the value of his service itself betroth her?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the value of his service can betroth her by itself, and starts quoting a ברייתא about betrothing with the value of a ride.
steps.simpleTranslation: And can she not be betrothed by the value of his service? But it was taught: 'Be betrothed by the value of my having let you ride on the donkey, or sit in a wagon or a boat.' She is not betrothed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש by asking why the value of the work cannot be the קידושין. It begins quoting a ברייתא, so this step is setting up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's opening case is about a ride already given. There she is not betrothed, because the value of the ride is already owed to him, like a loan. The challenge to ריש לקיש depends on how the ברייתא goes on from here.

keyTerms.meaning: Through the value or wage of a service
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
That I let you ride
A wagon

steps.confusionAlert: This first line of the ברייתא seems to agree with ריש לקיש, because she is not betrothed. That is because the ride already happened. The actual challenge comes as the ברייתא continues.

phrases.english: And by the value of his service, not?
phrases.notes: Meaning: why can't the value of his speaking or working count as the קידושין money?

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: 'By the value of my having let you ride on the donkey,'

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוֹשַׁבְתִּיךְ בְּקָרוֹן אוֹ בִּסְפִינָה – אֵינָהּ מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת.
phrases.english: 'of my having seated you in a wagon or in a boat,' she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's statement in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that a separate פרוטה is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the value of a service can be used for קידושין, then the work itself should be enough, and no extra פרוטה should be needed. The ברייתא is brought to test this.

steps.title: The value of a ride betroths her
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says she is betrothed 'by the value' of a ride on a donkey, wagon, or boat. You cannot say he gave a separate פרוטה, because the ברייתא says 'by the value.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says: 'Be betrothed by the value of my giving you a ride on a donkey, or seating you in a wagon or a boat,' she is betrothed. And if you say that here too he gave her something worth a פרוטה, the ברייתא says 'by the value.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא it began quoting in step 13. It then blocks the easy answer that he gave her a separate פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש said the service in our משנה is only a condition, and a real פרוטה does the betrothing. This ברייתא says the ride itself is what betroths her ('בשכר'). So it seems the value of a service can work as קידושין money, and that is a problem for ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: By the value of / as payment for
Wagon
And if you would say (the גמרא brings up a possible answer in order to reject it)
Something worth a פרוטה, the smallest amount that counts as money

phrases.english: By the value of my giving you a ride on a donkey,
or of my seating you in a wagon or in a boat —
she is betrothed.
And if you would say that here too
it is a case where he gave her something worth a פרוטה,
but it says 'by the value'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא הָכָא נָמֵי בְּדִיהַב לַהּ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה, וְהָא בִּשְׂכַר קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא and the challenge begun in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation that the משנה requires a separate פרוטה (step 12).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the woman is betrothed 'by the value' of the ride, so the service itself acts as the קידושין money, with no separate פרוטה needed.

steps.title: The court appraises his entertainment or work
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא says that if she asks him to sit with her, entertain, dance, or do building work, the court appraises it. If it is worth a פרוטה she is betrothed. Appraising only makes sense if the service itself betroths her, so this is a refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: If she says, 'Sit with me, and I will be betrothed to you,' or 'Entertain me,' 'Dance for me,' or 'Do work like this row of a building,' the court appraises it. If it is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed, and if not, she is not. And if you say that here too he gave her a פרוטה, the ברייתא says 'we appraise it.' This is a refutation of ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, stronger ברייתא against ריש לקיש. It ends with the word תיובתא, meaning it looks like a full refutation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a separate פרוטה did the betrothing, there would be no reason to appraise his service. The fact that the court checks whether the service is worth a פרוטה shows that the service itself is the קידושין money.

keyTerms.meaning: Together, in company
A row or layer of stones in a building
We appraise; the court estimates the value
A refutation; a challenge that seems to knock down a view

steps.confusionAlert: Here it is the woman who asks him for the service. The point is that his favor to her is treated like money he gives her, which is how קידושין normally works.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught in a ברייתא:
If she says, 'Sit with me together, and I will be betrothed to you,'
'Entertain me,' 'Dance for me,'
'Do work like this row of a building' —
phrases.notes: She points to a row of stones in a building and asks him to build one like it for her.

phrases.english: the court appraises it;

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ שָׁוֶה פְּרוּטָה – מְקוּדֶּשֶׁת,
phrases.english: if it is worth a פרוטה, she is betrothed,
and if not, she is not betrothed.
And if you would say that here too
it is a case where he gave her something worth a פרוטה,
but it says 'we appraise it'!
This is a refutation of ריש לקיש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger ברייתא to the challenge from step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation that the משנה requires a separate פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The court appraises the service to see if it reaches a פרוטה. That only makes sense if the service itself is the קידושין money.

steps.title: It depends on when payment for work becomes owed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers that the ברייתא and our משנה disagree about when payment for hired work becomes owed. The ברייתא holds it is owed only at the end, so the service can betroth. Our משנה holds it builds up from start to finish, so by the end it is just a debt, and a separate פרוטה is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש can say to you: The תנא of this ברייתא holds that payment for hired work is owed only at the end. Our תנא holds that payment for hired work builds up from the beginning to the end.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש defends himself. He says the ברייתות follow a different view than our משנה, so they do not disprove his explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If payment is owed only at the end, the value of the work becomes due all at once when he finishes, so it works like handing her money. If payment builds up the whole time, she slowly owes him more and more, so by the end it is an old debt, and a debt cannot be used for קידושין. That is why, in our משנה, he must also give a real פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiring; the payment owed for hired work
The 'outside' tanna, the tanna of a ברייתא
Payment for hire is owed only at the end of the work
Payment for hire builds up from the beginning of the work to the end

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties a קידושין question to a general money question: when does a worker's pay become owed? That decides whether his service counts like a gift of money or like an old debt.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש can say to you:
This tanna of the ברייתא holds:
payment for hired work is owed only at the end.
And our tanna holds:
payment for hired work builds up from the beginning to the end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the תיובתא of step 15 by separating the ברייתות from our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaitic disagreement: the sources follow different views about when payment for hired work becomes owed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות show that a service can always betroth, so ריש לקיש's separate פרוטה is wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתות hold that payment is owed only at the end, so the service works as money. Our משנה holds that it builds up into a debt, so a separate פרוטה is needed.

steps.title: Why did ריש לקיש choose the harder explanation?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what forced ריש לקיש to explain our משנה with the view that payment builds up over time, and to add a separate פרוטה. He could have explained the משנה like the ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what forced ריש לקיש to explain our משנה as holding that payment for work builds up from beginning to end, and as a case where he gave her a פרוטה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question that sets up the next move. Why not simply say the משנה agrees with the ברייתות, so the service itself betroths?
steps.deeperAnalysis: After step 16, both views are possible. Explaining the משנה like the ברייתות would be simpler and would not need an extra פרוטה. The גמרא wants to know what in the משנה pushed ריש לקיש away from that easier reading, and the answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: What forced him; his difficulty
To set up or explain a text as talking about a certain case or view

phrases.english: And what forced ריש לקיש
to explain our משנה
as holding that payment for work builds up from beginning to end,
and as a case where he gave her something?
phrases.notes: He means: gave her a separate פרוטה, as ריש לקיש said in step 12.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the choice ריש לקיש made in step 16 for our משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What in the משנה forced ריש לקיש to reject the simpler reading, where payment is owed only at the end and the service itself betroths her?

steps.title: The words 'on the condition' forced ריש לקיש's reading
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the wording of our משנה forced ריש לקיש. The משנה says 'על מנת' (on the condition) instead of 'בשכר' (by the value). That shows he already gave her a separate פרוטה, and the work is only a condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The משנה's wording bothered ריש לקיש. Why does it say 'on the condition'? It should have said 'by the value,' like the ברייתא. So we learn that any 'on the condition' is a case where he already gave her something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17: why did ריש לקיש not explain our משנה like the ברייתות? רבא says the word 'על מנת' in the משנה pushed him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות say 'בשכר' (by the value), which means the service itself is the money of the קידושין. Our משנה says 'על מנת' instead, which is the language of a condition. A condition only makes sense if something was already given, so ריש לקיש had to add a separate פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה was difficult for him (its wording bothered him)
Why specifically? Why this wording and not another?
On the condition: the language of a condition attached to something already given
By the value: the service itself counts as the payment
Learn from this (a conclusion drawn from the text)

steps.whatToRemember: In our משנה, 'על מנת' means a separate פרוטה was already given, and the work is only a condition. In the ברייתות, 'בשכר' means the work itself is the קידושין money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how one word ('על מנת' versus 'בשכר') can decide whether the service is the payment or just a condition.

phrases.english: Rava said:
The Mishnah was difficult for him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' means ריש לקיש. רבא is explaining what pushed him.

phrases.english: Why does it specifically teach 'on the condition'?
Let it teach 'by the value'!
Rather, learn from this:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל ״עַל מְנָת״ הֵיכָא דִּיהַב לַהּ הוּא.
phrases.english: Any 'on the condition' is a case where he already gave her something.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17 about why ריש לקיש explained the משנה the way he did.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What forced ריש לקיש to read the משנה as needing a separate פרוטה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's word 'על מנת' signals a condition on something already given, unlike 'בשכר' in the ברייתות.

steps.title: New משנה: betrothal on condition that the father agrees
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a man betroths a woman on the condition that his father will want it. If the father wants it, she is betrothed. If not, she is not. If the father dies, she is betrothed. If the son dies, we tell the father to say he does not want it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man says 'on the condition that my father will want it': if the father wants it, she is betrothed, and if not, she is not betrothed. If the father died, she is betrothed. If the son died, we teach the father to say that he does not want it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It gives the rule for a קידושין that depends on the man's father wanting it, plus two cases of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule is simple: the father's wish decides it. The death cases are the surprise. If the father dies, she is betrothed even though he never said anything. If the son dies, we advise the father to refuse, so the קידושין never took effect.

keyTerms.meaning: That my father will want it
She is betrothed
She is not betrothed
We teach / we instruct (we advise someone what to say)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אבא' here is the father of the man who is doing the betrothing. It is not the woman's father.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
'On the condition that my father will want it,'
phrases.notes: The man says this to the woman about his own father.

phrases.english: if the father wants it, she is betrothed;
and if not, she is not betrothed.
If the father died, she is betrothed.
If the son died,
we teach the father to say that he does not want it.
phrases.notes: That way the קידושין never took effect, so she won't need יבום or חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קידושין on condition of the father's wish depends on him. If the father dies, she is betrothed. If the son dies, the father is told to refuse.

steps.title: What does 'on the condition that my father will want' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly the condition 'that my father will want it' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'on the condition that my father will want it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by asking what the condition means. This sets up the next move, where it will test a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words could mean the father must actively say yes, or something else. The גמרא needs to pin this down because the death cases in the משנה depend on it.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא: the discussion of the משנה begins
What? What does it mean?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What does 'on the condition that my father will want it' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the condition stated in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of the condition 'that my father will want it.'

steps.title: It cannot mean 'until the father says yes'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to say the condition means the father must say yes. The middle case rejects this: if the father dies she is betrothed, even though he never said yes. So the גמרא begins a different explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means until the father says 'yes,' look at the middle case: if the father died, she is betrothed. But he never said 'yes'! Rather:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests a simple meaning of the condition and knocks it down using the משנה's own middle case. It ends with 'אלא' (rather), which sets up a new explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father had to say 'yes,' then a father who died silent never fulfilled the condition, so she should not be betrothed. Yet the משנה says she is betrothed. So the condition must mean something else, and the גמרא is about to explain what.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion that will be rejected
Yes
The middle clause of the משנה
But look: introduces the problem
Rather: a new explanation is coming

phrases.english: If you say it means until the father says 'yes,'
then say the middle clause:
If the father died, she is betrothed,
but he never said 'yes'!
Rather:

steps.triggerLanguage: אילימא עד דאמר אבא אין, אימא מציעתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests a possible answer to the question of step 20 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'שירצה אבא' means the father must actively say 'yes.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's middle case says she is betrothed when the father dies, even though he never said 'yes.' That contradicts a reading that requires his 'yes.'
